title: Knowledge check: Testing Tools and Setup

questions.prompt: In Testing Tools and Setup, which statement best describes Node.js built-in test runner?
options: Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.

Make behavior reproducible with assertions for a normal case, invalid input, boundary values and errors. Mock external side effects in unit tests and keep separate integration checks for real boundaries.
This option describes a different concept and does not define node.js built-in test runner (choice 2).
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
questions.answer_key: Make behavior reproducible with assertions for a normal case, invalid input, boundary values and errors. Mock external side effects in unit tests and keep separate integration checks for real boundaries.
questions.explanation: Make behavior reproducible with assertions for a normal case, invalid input, boundary values and errors. Mock external side effects in unit tests and keep separate integration checks for real boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Testing Tools and Setup?
options: Tests should exercise success paths, invalid inputs, permissions, boundary conditions, and dependency failures. Keep external side effects isolated and run repeatable checks in CI before deployment.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
questions.answer_key: Tests should exercise success paths, invalid inputs, permissions, boundary conditions, and dependency failures. Keep external side effects isolated and run repeatable checks in CI before deployment.
questions.explanation: Tests should exercise success paths, invalid inputs, permissions, boundary conditions, and dependency failures. Keep external side effects isolated and run repeatable checks in CI before deployment.

questions.prompt: A change related to Testing Tools and Setup appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
